findings.message: The CLI guard `import.meta.url !== `file://${process.argv[1]}`` compares a percent-encoded, symlink-resolved URL with a raw path. The two differ when the checkout path contains a space or other encoded character, or when it is reached through a symlink (Node realpaths the ESM main module, but argv[1] is only path.resolve'd). When they differ, `main()` never runs, nothing is printed, and the process exits 0, so the ✓auto retention and required-files check reports as passed without checking anything. Fix: compare with `pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href`, or move the parsers into a separate module that the CLI and the tests both import, so the CLI always runs `main()`.
findings.scenario: CI workspace at `/builds/my org/amax`, or a worktree reached through a symlinked `/tmp` → `node scripts/check-module-standard.mjs` with a module that has a personal table and no retention entry → exit 0, no output.

findings.message: [design] The fix for name-only tables matches `subjectName` columns by comparing the free-text name (lowercased and trimmed) with the requested person's name. A name does not identify a person. (1) Homonyms: an erasure anonymises the rows of everyone with the same name, and an access request (`buildPackage` uses the same `about()`) exports another person's records to the requester. A person hold also pauses the purge for the homonyms' rows. (2) Variants: 'Sam' vs 'Samantha', a maiden name, a missing middle name or a typo match nothing. Those rows stay out of the inventory, and the request still completes as 'Erased'. So name matching both over-reaches (data loss and disclosure) and under-reaches (rows left behind and reported as erased). Fix: give each name-bearing table an id column for the person (`owner_user_id` or an actor id) and match on that. If a name column must stay, list name-only hits as 'needs review' and keep them out of the automatic erase and the access export.
findings.scenario: Two people named 'Kasun Perera' each own presales.task rows. An erasure request for one of them is approved, and `about()` matches lower(owner_name) = 'kasun perera', so the other person's tasks are anonymised too. An access request for one exports both people's tasks. Separately, a task with owner_name 'Sam Test' is not found for the person 'Samantha Test', and that request completes as Erased.

findings.message: declaredFieldClasses builds one tenant-wide map keyed only by the normalised field name. It gives every field of a retention entry that entry's class, whatever module or table the field is on. Any event from any module that carries a field with the same name is then masked with that class. For example, a payroll entry with fields ['amount'] or ['name', 'base_salary'] under class 'pay' masks `amount` or `name` in finance and delivery webhooks. The earlier fix asked for masking from the emitting module's declared classes, not a global name map. Fix: key the classes by emitting module (the event-name prefix, or the manifest that emits it), and apply only that module's declared classes to its payloads.
findings.scenario: Payroll declares a retention entry for its payslip table with fields ['amount'] and class 'pay' → finance emits `finance.invoice.paid` {amount: 1200} → the webhook receiver gets {amount: {masked: true, class: 'pay'}}.

findings.message: Sharing the limiter through globalThis only works when the proxy and the app run in the same process, after the app has already called getDb(). On Vercel and Cloudflare (OpenNext), both required deploy targets, the proxy runs in a separate function or isolate. There the sink is always the no-op, so page 429s are never written to api.rate_limited and the 'Pages' row stays at 0. On k3s, 429s from before the first getDb() are also dropped. The previous finding asked for a recorder or a shared store. Fix: wire the rate-limit recorder in proxy.ts itself, or queue limited events somewhere the app drains, rather than relying on shared process memory.
findings.scenario: Deploy to Vercel with AMAX_RATE_PAGE_USER=5 → a user makes 10 page navigations in one minute → the proxy returns 429s, but api.rate_limited stays empty and Settings › API shows Pages: 0 requests limited.

findings.message: Dedupe for GitHub calls is now the only replay protection, because GitHub sends no timestamp. It depends on api.inbound rows still existing. This diff moves api.inbound deletion into the 032 purge, where a tenant's own period overrides the declared P90D. An Admin who shortens api.inbound's period with set_retention_period also shortens how long a captured signed GitHub body can't be replayed. Fix: keep the dedupe key in its own store with a fixed minimum lifetime, outside the retention purge, or give api.inbound a floor (a statutory-style minimum) that tenant periods can't go below.
findings.scenario: Admin sets the period for 'Incoming webhook calls' to P1D → the purge deletes yesterday's api.inbound rows → a captured GitHub push (same body, same signature, fresh x-github-delivery) is replayed → accepted as a new verified event.

findings.message: The chat retention fix (idle → `start.at: ['updated_at']`) was a major, but this diff ships no test with it. Nothing shows that a conversation idle for 91 days is now due and that one idle for 89 days is not. Under the old declaration, either would have been kept until day 180. Fix: add a table-driven purge test that drives purgeDue or previewPurge over conversations last updated 89, 91 and 179 days ago. It must fail against the old `idle: 'P90D'` declaration.
findings.scenario: Revert the line to `start: { at: [], idle: 'P90D' }` → every test in this diff still passes.

findings.message: [design] 'Rules checked tonight' and 'Every rule could be checked' come only from `previewPurge().failed`. The purge doesn't touch subject or subjectName columns unless a hold is active, so a rule whose subject column is broken previews fine. Yet every access and erasure request now refuses to open on it (`assertChecked`). The screen says everything is fine while privacy requests are blocked. The new test encodes this gap (`purge=false` cases skip the overview assertion). Fix: have the overview also try each searchable rule's `about()` arm (for example, count with an empty match) and show those failures as unknown or blocking requests.
findings.scenario: A retention entry has subject: ['no_such_column']. The overview ticket reads 'N of N', 'Every rule could be checked', and the lede gives no warning. Opening any request then fails with 'could not check Broken subject'.

findings.message: This adds a second local `chatOnly()` guard beside the existing one used for credential tools (`create_api_credential`). The two differ in message and could drift on which sources count as chat. Share one helper.

The SQL scan reads `add [column]` but not `alter table … rename column x to <personal name>`. It also skips columns copied by `create table … (like other)`, because CONSTRAINT treats `like` as a constraint. Either way a personal column reaches a table and the check passes silently. Read renames and treat `like` as unreadable.
findings.scenario: `alter table people.visit rename column ref to visitor_email;` with no retention entry → check passes.

findings.message: The lede tells the Admin to 'add it in Secrets', but the screen these secrets live on is 'Connections and keys' (the page note and the README both say so). packages/api/README.md also still hard-codes '5 minutes', 'retried 5 times' and 'after 5 deliveries' instead of naming REPLAY_WINDOW_MS, RETRY and MAX_FAILURES.

[design] The proxy and app now share the limiter through `globalThis`, which only works when both bundles run in the same process (the k3s and standalone image). On Vercel, the proxy runs as its own routing function, and Cloudflare/OpenNext runs it in a separate worker. There, `ensureRateLimits` sets the env limits but the sink stays the no-op, because `rateLimitRecorder` is only wired in `getDb()`. Page 429s are never recorded in api.rate_limited, and the 'Pages' row reads 0. PRODUCT.md requires the app to deploy unchanged to all three hosts. The fix covers only one host: wire a recorder inside proxy.ts itself, or record through a store the proxy can reach.
findings.scenario: On Vercel, a user exceeds AMAX_RATE_PAGE_USER and the proxy answers 429. The sink is a no-op, so api.rate_limited gets no 'page' row and Settings › API shows Pages: 0 requests limited.

findings.message: [design] The previous finding asked to mask from the declared classes and fail closed on fields with no class. The fix adds the declared map but keeps the regex as the only fallback: a payload field that no retention entry or tool `sensitive` declares, and that no pattern matches, is sent unmasked. The declared map is also keyed globally by field name, not by the emitting module's event, so the mask depends on whether any installed module happens to list that column in a retention entry. Fix: give each emitted event a declared field classification and refuse to send (or mask) fields without one.
findings.scenario: An event payload carries `probation_outcome` (performance) or `netAmount` (pay) from a module that lists neither field in a retention entry or a tool's `sensitive`. classOf finds no declared class, the regex doesn't match ('netAmount' doesn't match /net_?pay/), and the value is POSTed in clear to the external receiver.

findings.message: retentionEntries decides whether an entry is findable by slicing the text from one `table:` to the next. An entry that writes `subject` before `table` (`{ subject: [...], table: "x" }`) has its subject credited to the previous entry, so the check can pass an entry with no subject or fail one that has one. Parse each object literal instead.
findings.scenario: The entry `{ label: 'X', subject: ['id'], table: 'm.b' }` follows `{ table: 'm.a', fields: [...] }`. m.a reads as findable and m.b as not findable.
